# R06 strict stop lane design fixtures

`cases.json` freezes the [MuJoCo owner socket contract](../../../docs/mujoco/interfaces/socket.md#r06-managed-stop-contract-design-target). It is a design matrix, not a claim that the current C++ server passes. MuJoCo CTest owns the socket, engine, deduplication, stop-lane, scene and direct-launch cases. EOS tests own Dispatcher admission, outer deadline, stop-before-terminate/reap, and durable no-replay cases. IsOS tests own reverse dependent process shutdown and deployed run state. The cross-owner replay must join those results; MuJoCo CTest alone cannot prove EOS or IsOS behavior. Each owner should record exact case IDs, results and elapsed monotonic time in `logs/test/<run-id>/` for independent review.

The `fence` cases require a deterministic barrier at engine command commit, not timing-only sleeps. `dedup` cases include identical movement replay after an epoch change and a changed-epoch conflict, preserving R05 precedence. `concurrent` cases fill all eight main ingress slots with partial frames, then use the independent `.stop` listener; two partial stop-socket clients also exercise its 500 ms successful-connect-to-classification bound. The queued-partial case fills all three companion ingress workers and checks that a fourth partial frame retains its 250 ms accept-relative deadline while queued. A fresh `generation_id` per managed child rejects delayed movement and companion stop requests from the previous child even when `stop_epoch` resets to `"0"`. `stop_result` cases independently inject base and arm failures. `capture` cases block EGL/JPEG after a snapshot to prove the stop path does not need the render lock. `lifecycle` cases verify timeout, crash, force-reap, socket cleanup, and restart without replay of an uncertain old command. Direct-launch cases preserve historical `2.0.0` behavior.

Run `python3 tests/fixtures/strict_stop_lane/check.py` for static fixture and EN/CN contract checks. This does not establish runtime stop safety.
